title: KL divergence on a finite space as a sum of log-ratios
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite discrete measurable space, and let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be finite measures on $\Omega$. If there is a point $\omega \in \Omega$ with $\nu(\{\omega\}) = 0$ but $\mu(\{\omega\}) \neq 0$, then the Kullback–Leibler divergence is infinite:
\[
  D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu \,\|\, \nu) = \infty.
\]
Otherwise,
\[
  D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu \,\|\, \nu)
  = \left(
      \sum_{\omega \in \Omega}
        \mu(\{\omega\}) \,\log\!\frac{\mu(\{\omega\})}{\nu(\{\omega\})}
      + \nu(\Omega) - \mu(\Omega)
    \right)_{+},
\]
where each $\mu(\{\omega\})$, $\nu(\{\omega\})$, $\mu(\Omega)$, $\nu(\Omega)$ denotes the (real-valued) mass of the indicated set and $(x)_{+} = \max(x, 0)$ is the nonnegative part.
hypotheses_covered: Ω is a finite discrete measurable space
μ and ν are finite measures on Ω
case split: some singleton has ν-mass zero and nonzero μ-mass gives value ∞
otherwise the value is the nonnegative part (ENNReal.ofReal) of the sum of μ-mass times log of the mass ratio over all points, plus total ν-mass minus total μ-mass
